_doc: Justified React-vs-Rust differences. Key: <case>|<facet>|<fact> or <case>|<facet>|* for a by-design structural difference. Facets: tree, role, aria, data, class, attr. An unlisted drift fact fails the parity test; a listed entry that no longer drifts also fails (stale).

entries.tabs|tree|*: Rust tabs are CSS-only (radio input + label + panel, no JS); React tabs are a button tablist with roving focus. Different element tree by design (crates/cascivo-html/tests/nav.rs).
entries.tabs|role|*: React uses role=tablist/tab/tabpanel via JS-managed ARIA; the CSS-only Rust tabs expose native radio semantics and role=group panels.
entries.tabs|aria|*: React aria-selected/aria-controls on buttons vs Rust aria-labelledby on panels; state is the radio's :checked instead of aria-selected.
entries.tabs|data|*: React data-state/data-value drive styling; Rust marks radio mode with data-radio and uses :checked.
entries.tabs|class|*: Class contract differs only where the element tree differs (list/trigger button vs input/label/content).
entries.tabs|attr|*: Native radio plumbing in Rust (type, name, for, checked, ids) versus React tabindex/type=button/ids.
